component_records.title: Bid administration and RFP communications control
component_records.description: A single named bid coordinator owns all communication with MoDOT during the procurement: every question or comment about the RFP is submitted by e-mail to the designated RFP mailbox by the date and time listed in Section 1E, and no MoDOT employee is contacted by any other method. The coordinator logs each question, its submission timestamp and MoDOT's posted response, and circulates the answers to the writing team so the proposal reflects them. The same coordinator controls the submission calendar so the proposal is filed within the RFP's stated deadlines, with time treated as of the essence, and confirms receipt notification before standing down. This component is internal bid-team effort and carries no cost in the price page.

component_records.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: A named project manager runs the study against a finalized work plan that details every task, the resources assigned and the schedule, and that is submitted to MoDOT for approval, recognising MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans. The team facilitates a kick-off meeting with MoDOT to review the work plan, scope and schedule and to establish a protocol for regular ongoing communications and coordination, then holds quarterly project status meetings (in person or online) reviewing progress for the previous period and anticipated work for the next. E-mail and phone communication with MoDOT contacts provides ongoing progress updates between meetings, and the team fully coordinates its activities with the Construction and Materials Division and makes advice and information on matters covered by the Agreement available to that Division as the work progresses. The team consults MHTC's representative on any concerns about administration of the services, and all RFP events and meetings are scheduled within the 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Central window.

component_records.title: Schedule, milestone and reporting control
component_records.description: A milestone plan fixes the 15-month contract period from the November 2024 start to the 2 February 2026 contract end and final invoice, and drives every dated deliverable: the data management plan, the 25 April 2025 demonstration of AI/ML drafting, the mid-point interim presentation, the draft synthesis report and research summary, and the final report, summary, presentation and user manual. Quarterly updates on work accomplished are submitted on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December for the duration of the project, timed to feed the SPR Quarterly Report the Division submits to FHWA at each fiscal quarter end. An interim presentation near the mid-point updates MoDOT on progress and project direction. The plan is built so that all work completes inside the not-to-exceed $175,000 and the quoted fees, and so that the proposal is submitted within the RFP's stated deadlines.

component_records.title: Literature search and review of state DOT practice
component_records.description: Task 2 delivers a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes, covering published research, agency reports and peer DOT deployments, and summarising what has worked, what has failed and what is transferable to MoDOT's metes-and-bounds and deed-based description work. The review is delivered as a structured findings matrix plus a narrative chapter that feeds the synthesis report, and it is presented at the kick-off and interim meetings so MoDOT can steer the proof of concept.

component_records.title: Data management plan and data handling
component_records.description: Within two weeks of the kick-off meeting the team submits a Data Management Plan to MoDOT that describes the anticipated formats of the study's data and related files and commits to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats (for example plain-text/CSV, PDF/A and open geospatial formats) so the data retains maximum future utility for MoDOT. The plan also sets out storage, retention and access arrangements consistent with MHTC ownership of all data and deliverables, and is maintained as a living document through the project.

component_records.title: LLD generation engine and IS approval gate
component_records.description: The team configures an AI/ML drafting engine that takes MoDOT's parcel, right-of-way plan and deed inputs and produces a first-draft legal land description using MHTC parameters, applying metes and bounds for partial acquisitions and reproducing the last deed of record verbatim where a property is acquired in its entirety, and conforming to MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2. Before any proof-of-concept work begins, the team names the program used to develop the LLDs and submits it, with version, licensing, hosting and security documentation, for MoDOT Information Systems approval, and does not proceed to Task 3c until that approval is given. The application is built only on approved technologies: a currently supported .NET 6.0 or above release (or .NET Framework 4.8 or above where specifically needed), the MVC, Razor Pages or Web API framework, and the approved languages C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, with any large-scale Python use put to the BRPT for approval. It is a browser-based web application requiring no client-side software beyond a modern browser, tested against the latest IS-approved browsers, with library dependencies reviewed and updated annually, and it uses no third-party tool or component that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior BRPT and IS management approval.

component_records.title: Hosted data layer, accessibility and security compliance
component_records.description: The drafting application runs on an on-premise database on Oracle 19C (or the latest supported SQL Server where MoDOT IS Data Service Management approves), with no PII stored in any table unless a specific business need is established and approved by the IS Cyber Security Team. All web screens meet the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508 and WCAG 2.1 at AA, verified by automated and manual accessibility testing before the demonstration. The application uses no text, diagrams, photographs, audio, multimedia, source code, script or graphics from another author's web pages unless that author explicitly permits free copying or arrangements are made, and vendor logos or branding are removed wherever a supported, licensed option exists to do so.

component_records.title: Proof of concept: AI-drafted LLDs with ROW staff review
component_records.description: Task 3c demonstrates how the AI/ML technology creates draft legal land descriptions for a variety of property types, including partial acquisitions requiring metes and bounds and whole-property acquisitions requiring verbatim deed descriptions, with MoDOT ROW staff reviewing each draft and providing structured feedback on improvements. The team demonstrates the AI writing a legal land description live on 25 April 2025 for MoDOT feedback, then iterates the parameters, prompts and review workflow against that feedback. Each demonstration round produces a scored comparison of AI draft versus staff-edited final, so MoDOT can judge whether the first draft is useful in practice.

component_records.title: Training, user manual and change support
component_records.description: Once the system is developed and finalized, the team trains MoDOT ROW staff on its use and delivers a user manual staff can reference afterwards, covering input preparation, running a draft, reviewing and editing output, and the metes-and-bounds and deed-verbatim rules the tool enforces. Training is delivered in a train-the-trainer format with recorded sessions and a question-and-answer clinic, and the manual is supplied in editable and print-ready form so MoDOT can maintain it. Training and the manual are completed by the 25 July 2025 milestone so staff can use the tool before the final report.

component_records.title: Synthesis report, final report, summary and presentation
component_records.description: The team prepares a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary that are complete final products except for revisions arising from MoDOT's review, together with the accompanying documentation identified as beneficial during the study. The final report details every task completed and all findings generated during the project, and is accompanied by a 1-2 page research summary stating the project objectives, findings and conclusions and by a presentation for MoDOT staff. All documents follow the Publication Guidelines and summary template and are delivered in the required electronic formats, with MHTC retaining ownership of every report and exhibit.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and insurance obligations
component_records.description: A compliance register is maintained from award to close-out covering each contractual obligation. The awarded contract incorporates the RFP's contract provisions, and the Offeror accepts that MHTC may cancel the award and select a different Offeror if post-award terms cannot be agreed; written clarifications issued by MHTC govern over conflicting requirements, and any change to the Agreement is made by formal contract amendment signed by both authorised representatives. The Offeror does not release any material or report to the public without MHTC's prior consent, does not assign, delegate or novate any interest without MHTC's prior written consent, and remains ultimately responsible for the quality and performance of all services regardless of subcontractors. Every subcontract incorporates Section (3), paragraph I of the Agreement, and the Offeror takes any action the Commission directs to enforce those provisions, including sanctions for noncompliance. The Offeror complies with Missouri Executive Order 07-13 and certifies that every assigned employee is eligible and authorised to work in the United States, and provides by sworn affidavit its enrolment and participation in a federal work-authorisation program such as E-Verify, the E-Verify MOU for the employees proposed, and an affirmation that it does not knowingly employ unauthorised aliens; where the entity is a sole proprietorship or partnership, each sole proprietor and general partner provides affirmative proof of lawful presence under Section 208.009, RSMo, and the affiant certifies sound mind and personal knowledge of the facts under Section 285.530, RSMo. All documents, reports and exhibits produced at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC property, and MHTC may reproduce and use the products without royalties or fees. The Offeror does not disclose confidential factual matters to third parties except as required by statute, ordinance or court order or as authorised by MHTC's representative, and notifies MHTC immediately of any request for such information. Working papers and records are maintained and made available at no charge to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor at all reasonable times during the term and for three years from final payment. The Offeror carries General Liability and Automobile Liability insurance of not less than $500,000 per person per occurrence and $3,000,000 per occurrence in the aggregate, maintains a Missouri State Workmen's Compensation policy or equivalent, and can provide certificates of insurance meeting or approaching these coverages before contract signing. The Offeror also commits to direct hiring of minorities and women and to MBE/WBE participation of 10% and 5% respectively through subcontractors, suppliers or joint ventures.

component_records.title: Cost estimate and price page
component_records.description: The Offeror completes the Section (4) Price Page with a cost estimate that covers all costs for providing the services in accordance with the RFP, broken out by Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost, and Miscellaneous, with a Total, and with any Miscellaneous costs itemised on an attached sheet. The estimate is built to the $175,000 not-to-exceed ceiling for the full 15-month period, and the Offeror agrees to provide the services at the fees quoted under the terms of the RFP. A detailed budget is developed with MoDOT after award, consistent with the Price Page.

items.text: The RFP is issued by the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC) for the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT), with the study coordinated by the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division.

MoDOT's Right of Way staff currently must write legal land descriptions that accurately define land areas or rights to be acquired, conveyed or leased, using metes and bounds, lot calls or 1/4 - 1/4 calls, and such descriptions can be long and tedious to write.

Realty rights acquired or conveyed by MHTC must be described by metes and bounds unless the property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.

Before a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or similar document is presented to the grantor, a professional land surveyor must review the property description to verify the parcel corresponds with the right of way plans and that the plans correspond with survey information gathered by the surveyor.
Descriptions prepared on behalf of MHTC must meet the requirements in the MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2.

The business driver is to determine the usefulness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to produce a "first draft" legal land description using MHTC parameters that MoDOT's Right of Way staff could review and edit.

MoDOT's fiscal year runs from July 1 to June 30, and quarterly project updates feed the Statewide Planning and Research (SPR) Quarterly Report the Construction and Materials Division submits to FHWA at the end of each fiscal quarter.
The Offeror must conduct the TR202504 research study "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions" for MHTC and MoDOT, with a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000.

The core deliverable is a proof of concept (Task 3c) demonstrating how AI/ML technology will create draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and providing feedback on improvements.
The Offeror must conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes (Task 2).
The Offeror must train ROW staff on the finalized system and provide a user manual for staff to reference (Task 4).
The Offeror must deliver a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary (Task 5) and a final report, a 1-2 page research summary, and a presentation for MoDOT staff (Task 6).
The contract period is 15 months, with the project schedule estimated to start November 1, 2024 and the final invoice due and contract ending 2/2/2026.

The Offeror must submit a Data Management Plan to MoDOT within 2 weeks after the kick-off meeting, describing anticipated data formats and how platform-independent, non-proprietary formats will be used to ensure maximum future utility of the data.
Proposals are due to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central, and are not considered submitted until notification of receipt, which should be sent by noon the same day.

All questions or comments must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. Central, the only acceptable contact method; contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is prohibited and cause for disqualification.
MoDOT posts its responses to questions and comments publicly on 7/31/2024 and notifies submitters about project selection or interviews on 9/18/2024.
After a responsiveness determination, proposals will be evaluated against criteria established by the Technical Advisory Committee, and the award goes to the Offeror providing the best proposal.

The Work Plan must be a narrative description of how the Offeror will work with MoDOT to fulfill project-specific requirements, limited to no longer than ten (10) pages with font size no less than 12 points, excluding forms and resumes.

The proposal must be submitted as one combined PDF in this order: Proposal Submission Form; optional one-page Cover Letter; Body of Proposal (work plan and project schedule); Personnel; Organization's Project Experience; Team Member Experience; and Organization's Client References.
The proposal must identify experience in offering the requested services during the past three years and list at least three client officials from the past three years as references.
The Offeror must present how the AI/ML will create draft LLDs on 4/25/2025 for MoDOT feedback, and after adjustments create the manual and train ROW staff by 7/25/2025.

Services are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, and the Offeror must submit a proposed cost estimate on the Section (4) Price Page covering Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost, and Miscellaneous, with a detailed budget developed later.
Before work begins on the proof of concepts, the Offeror must name the program used to develop the LLDs, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve it before Task 3c may proceed.

Applications must be built on approved technologies: a currently supported .NET 6.0 or above release (or .NET Framework 4.8 or above where specifically needed), MVC, Razor Pages or Web API for web applications, and approved languages C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, with large-scale Python use requiring BRPT approval.

Vendors may not use third-party tools or software that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team (BRPT) and IS management.

On-premise databases must run on Oracle 19C or the latest supported SQL Server (SQL Server 2016 or higher only with MoDOT IS Data Service Management approval), no client-side software other than a modern browser may be required, and no PII may be stored without a specific business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval.
All web applications must meet the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508 and adhere to WCAG 2.1 at 'AA' level of conformance.

All documents, reports and exhibits produced at MHTC's direction remain MHTC property, and the Offeror must keep working papers available to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor for three years from final payment, with MHTC free to reproduce and use the products without royalties.

The RFP refers bidders to documents not included in it—the Proposal Submission Form, the Standard Research Agreement, the Publication Guidelines and summary template, the price page template, and CCO Form CM09 (Approved 04/11, Revised 03/20)—all available at https://www.modot.org/information-researchers.
Questions and comments must go only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov, and contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is cause for disqualification.
The study is coordinated by the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division, which is the Division the Offeror must coordinate with and report to.
MoDOT's fiscal year runs 1 July to 30 June and quarterly project updates feed the SPR Quarterly Report submitted to FHWA at the end of each fiscal quarter.
The project schedule is estimated to start 1 November 2024 and the contract ends 2 February 2026.
MoDOT Right of Way staff currently write legal land descriptions by hand using metes and bounds, lot calls or 1/4-1/4 calls, and the business driver is a reviewable first draft.

The RFP refers bidders to a Standard Research Agreement, Publication Guidelines, price page template and CCO Form CM09 held on the MoDOT information-researchers web page rather than in the RFP itself.

The MHTC parameters the AI/ML draft must apply are assumed to be the metes-and-bounds, lot-call and 1/4-1/4 call conventions and EPG Section 236.4.6.2 rules described in the RFP, to be confirmed with MoDOT at kick-off.

The proof of concept is assumed to cover a sample of roughly 10-20 parcels spanning partial acquisitions, whole-property acquisitions and both urban and rural descriptions, demonstrated live and with recorded outputs.
Training is assumed to be two half-day sessions for up to 20 ROW staff, delivered remotely with an on-site option, plus a recorded session and an editable user manual.
The listed milestone dates are treated as binding, with the data management plan due two weeks after the kick-off meeting and no later than 4 December 2024, whichever falls first.
The $175,000 cap is assumed to be a firm ceiling covering all phases, travel and deliverables for the full 15-month term, with no optional or separately priced work.
The database platform is assumed to be Oracle 19C on MoDOT on-premise infrastructure, with SQL Server used only if MoDOT IS Data Service Management directs it.
The literature review is assumed to cover all 50 state DOTs plus published research from the last ten years, delivered as a findings matrix and narrative chapter.
The interim presentation is assumed to fall in month eight of the 15-month schedule, around June 2025, and the final presentation is assumed to be delivered virtually to MoDOT staff.

The named LLD-generation program is assumed to be a commercial or open-source large-language-model tool whose licensing places no responsibility on MoDOT, submitted to MoDOT IS with version, hosting and security documentation at kick-off.

The Publication Guidelines, summary template, Price Page, Proposal Submission Form and Standard Research Agreement are assumed to be the versions currently posted on the MoDOT information-researchers web page and will be obtained and followed as issued.
The MBE/WBE participation levels of 10% and 5% are treated as aspirational targets that will be reported but not contractually guaranteed.
Confidential factual matters are assumed to be marked as confidential by MHTC at the time of delivery, and any third-party request for them will be reported to MHTC within one business day.

Exhibits A and B (sworn affidavits) not in the RFP. The RFP requires a sworn affidavit of work-authorisation enrolment and, for sole proprietors and general partners, an affidavit of lawful presence on forms attached as Exhibit A and Exhibit B, but neither exhibit is in the document. The bid team cannot confirm the exact attestations, notarisation fields or classification boxes it must complete, and a defective or missing affidavit is a responsiveness problem at submission rather than a delivery problem. The exhibits are listed as referenced documents absent from the PDF, and the requirements around them (R115-R119, R152-R165) are detailed and form-specific. Severity is high because a missing or wrongly executed affidavit can disqualify the proposal.

MoDOT IS approval of the named LLD program gates the proof of concept. Task 3c cannot start until MoDOT Information Systems approves the named program used to develop the LLDs, and the RFP does not say what documentation must accompany the name or what criteria IS applies. If approval is slow or refused, the 25 April 2025 live demonstration and the 25 July 2025 training milestone both slip, and the fixed 2 February 2026 contract end leaves little room to recover. The proposed solution assumes a commercial or open-source LLM tool with no licensing burden on MoDOT, which is an assumption, not a confirmed approval. The gate is mandatory and sits directly in front of the core deliverable (R051, R052), and the RFP leaves the approval criteria and turnaround undefined. Likelihood is medium because it turns on MoDOT IS behaviour the RFP does not settle.

Fixed $175,000 ceiling over 15 months with undefined scope. The study is capped at a not-to-exceed $175,000 for a 15-month engagement covering literature review, an AI/ML build, a proof of concept, training, a user manual and four report deliverables, and the RFP does not say whether the cap includes travel, the on-site training option or the open-ended 'accompanying documentation identified as beneficial'. If the proof of concept needs more parcels or more iteration than assumed, the bidder absorbs the cost or cuts scope and quality. The cap is firm and the scope items that drive effort (number of parcels, training volume, open-ended documentation) are all left open by the RFP. Severity is high because a research study of this breadth at a fixed ceiling can overrun by more than a quarter if scope grows.

MHTC parameters and EPG Section 236.4.6.2 not defined in the RFP. The AI/ML draft must apply 'MHTC parameters' and meet MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2, but neither the parameters nor the EPG section is in the RFP. The proposed solution assumes the parameters are the metes-and-bounds, lot-call and 1/4-1/4 conventions described in the RFP and will confirm them at kick-off. If the real rules are more detailed, the drafting engine's rule set, prompts and validation logic are rebuilt after the proof of concept, which is exactly when there is least schedule left. The governing technical standard is referenced but absent, and the solution's own assumption list flags it as an inference. Severity is high because the rule set is the core of the product; likelihood is medium because the RFP does describe the three description methods.

Standard Research Agreement and contract provisions not available. The awarded contract incorporates the Standard Research Agreement and contract provisions that are not in the RFP, and MHTC may cancel the award if post-award terms cannot be agreed. The bidder is therefore pricing and committing to terms it has not read, including insurance, records, confidentiality and flow-down obligations, and could lose the award after selection over a term it would have negotiated up front. The agreement is referenced but absent, and R098 lets MHTC cancel the award if terms cannot be agreed. Severity is high because the loss is the whole contract; likelihood is medium because most terms are likely standard.

Data Management Plan deadline conflicts (12/4/2024 vs. two weeks after kick-off). The RFP fixes the Data Management Plan at 12/4/2024 in one place and at two weeks after the kick-off meeting in another, while the kick-off itself is to be scheduled on 11/15/2024. If the kick-off slips, the two rules diverge and the team can miss a contractual deliverable date in the first month of the contract, damaging credibility on a study whose whole value rests on data handling. The proposed solution resolves this by taking whichever date falls first, which is a bid-side assumption MoDOT has not agreed to. The conflict is explicit in the RFP (R034 vs. R047) and the kick-off date is itself listed as 'to be scheduled', so the two deadlines will diverge as soon as the kick-off moves. Impact is limited to one early deliverable, absorbable with rework.

Proof-of-concept scope (property count and types) left open. The RFP requires a demonstration on 'a variety of properties' without saying how many or which types, and the solution assumes roughly 10-20 parcels across partial and whole-property acquisitions, urban and rural. If MoDOT expects a larger or harder sample, the demonstration effort and the review cycle grow well beyond the priced assumption, and the 25 April 2025 date is fixed. The scope is undefined in the RFP and the solution's parcel count is an explicit inference. Likelihood is high because MoDOT ROW staff will naturally want broad coverage once they see the first drafts.

Training and user manual scope undefined. The RFP requires training of ROW staff and a user manual but does not state the number of staff, number of sessions, delivery mode, duration or manual format. The solution assumes two half-day remote sessions for up to 20 staff plus a recorded session and an editable manual. If MoDOT expects on-site, repeated or larger-audience training, the travel and staff time are unbudgeted inside a fixed ceiling. Both the training volume and the manual format are open in the RFP, and the solution's figures are inferences. Impact is material rework and cost but absorbable within contingency.

Publication Guidelines, summary template and Price Page not supplied. The final report and research summary must follow Publication Guidelines and a summary template, and the cost estimate must be on a Section (4) Price Page, but none of these documents is in the RFP. The bid team risks submitting a price page in the wrong structure or a report format that MoDOT rejects at review, forcing rework late in the schedule when the 2 February 2026 end date is fixed. These are referenced documents absent from the PDF and the solution assumes the currently posted versions are correct. Impact is rework of priced deliverables rather than project failure.

Insurance limits and MBE/WBE participation treated as soft requirements.
